principle: AUREN owns orchestration semantics; providers supply inference and native capabilities

chatgpt.important: Do not model ordinary ChatGPT chat as a local subprocess provider. Use Codex in ChatGPT, an approved MCP app, or the API when execution is required.

chatgpt_web.current_gap: The remote operator server and ChatGPT tool-level OAuth metadata/challenge are implemented, but AUREN does not host the OAuth authorization server. An external IdP must support authorization-code PKCE S256, resource/audience propagation, and CIMD or DCR. The endpoint is not deployed or live-tested, and no ChatGPT plugin is published.
next_steps: Configure and verify an OAuth 2.1 identity provider with PKCE S256, resource/audience claims, issuer discovery and CIMD or DCR.
Deploy the remote service behind TLS with a persistent host and verify ChatGPT OAuth linking and per-tool scopes.
Complete ChatGPT plugin/app packaging, privacy/support information and live acceptance.

chatgpt_desktop_codex.current_gap: Codex remote MCP setup is documented and the shared remote service is implemented. No live Codex app/desktop registration, ChatGPT OAuth linking or desktop acceptance run is recorded.
next_steps: Register the remote MCP endpoint in Codex app/CLI and verify the authenticated tool catalog.
Run a read-only task and a sandboxed task through AUREN; verify cancellation, evidence and exact-head gates.
Complete ChatGPT app/connector packaging if ChatGPT Chat/Work distribution is required.

codex_cli.current_gap: Remote MCP registration instructions are documented. A successful live connection, OAuth flow and tool acceptance run are not recorded.
next_steps: Run codex mcp add auren --url https://<host>/mcp and verify with codex mcp list.
Complete the host's OAuth flow and verify scope-filtered tool discovery.
Run disposable-repository acceptance for task submit/status/cancel/evidence.

codex_app.current_gap: The shared Codex MCP configuration path is documented, but the app has not been connected to a deployed AUREN endpoint or live-tested.
next_steps: Register AUREN in Codex app MCP settings.
Verify OAuth, scopes, task acceptance and operator tools.
Run desktop-specific acceptance for long-running tasks and cancellation.

claude_chat_web.current_gap: Claude web supports custom remote MCP connectors. AUREN's remote endpoint and OAuth resource-server path are implemented, but the external OAuth authorization server, deployment and Claude live connection are not complete.
next_steps: Configure the external OAuth provider for Claude's DCR/OAuth flow and AUREN scopes.
Add the remote connector in Claude Settings > Connectors.
Verify per-tool scopes and ensure task execution remains on the AUREN host.

claude_code_cli.current_gap: Remote HTTP registration is documented, but OAuth discovery, CLI connection and permission-mode acceptance have not been tested against an installed Claude Code version.
next_steps: Register with claude mcp add --transport http auren https://<host>/mcp.
Verify OAuth and /mcp discovery.
Run read-only and guarded task acceptance with the AUREN host policy.

claude_desktop.current_gap: Claude Desktop supports remote connectors through Settings > Connectors. AUREN's server is implemented but not deployed or tested. The remote connector submits work to the AUREN host; it does not grant local Desktop filesystem access.
next_steps: Add AUREN as a remote connector in Settings > Connectors, not as a local desktop_config.json server.
Complete OAuth and verify read/write tool scopes.
Test Claude Code's local Code workflow separately from Desktop chat connectors.

claude_vscode.current_gap: Remote MCP registration is documented, but no deployed endpoint or VS Code extension live smoke test is recorded.
next_steps: Register AUREN through Claude Code MCP settings.
Verify tool discovery, OAuth and permission prompts.
Test editor changes and remote task handoff separately.

visual_studio_ide.current_gap: Visual Studio itself supports remote MCP in Copilot Agent mode and has a documented .mcp.json setup. No AUREN Visual Studio connection, OAuth sign-in or tool acceptance run is recorded. This is not a Claude Code for Visual Studio extension.
next_steps: Add AUREN to solution-level .mcp.json and enable it in Copilot Agent mode.
Complete OAuth and verify read/write scope filtering.
Run Visual Studio-specific task, cancellation, approval and evidence acceptance.

gemini_cli.current_gap: Gemini CLI supports Streamable HTTP MCP and registration is documented. Google has moved some consumer Gemini CLI/Code Assist tiers to Antigravity; plan-specific availability must be checked. No live AUREN OAuth or Gemini CLI acceptance is recorded.
next_steps: Use gemini mcp add --transport http auren https://<host>/mcp where Gemini CLI remains available.
For consumer tiers migrated to Antigravity, use the Antigravity CLI entry and serverUrl configuration.
Complete OAuth and run task/status/evidence/cancellation acceptance.

gemini_code_assist_vscode.current_gap: Gemini Code Assist Agent mode in VS Code can load MCP servers through Gemini settings and the Gemini CLI integration. No AUREN connection or live test exists. Some consumer plans have migrated to Antigravity.
next_steps: Add the remote AUREN server to ~/.gemini/settings.json under mcpServers.
Test the supported Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise agent mode separately from Gemini CLI.
For migrated consumer plans, use Antigravity CLI or IDE and its serverUrl configuration.

cursor.current_gap: A Cursor rule and remote MCP setup example are now present. OAuth configuration, local Agent, Cloud Agent and remote SSH acceptance have not been tested.
next_steps: Add the endpoint in .cursor/mcp.json or global Cursor MCP settings.
Complete OAuth and verify tool allowlists/approval prompts.
Run separate local Agent, Cloud Agent, SSH and self-hosted worker acceptance.

groq_api.current_gap: No Groq provider adapter, model catalog, GROQ_API_KEY allowlist, timeout/retry contract, or live model conformance test exists. OpenAI-compatible does not mean every API feature is identical.
next_steps: Add a dedicated API provider adapter using https://api.groq.com/openai/v1.
Allow only the required secret through the secret broker/environment policy.
Implement capability/model discovery, structured tool-call normalization, usage/cost capture, retry budgets and unsupported-feature handling.
Run paired quality, latency, cost and safety tests before enabling routing.

grok_chat_web.current_gap: Grok web chat has no AUREN-native repository skill, local process, or repo execution adapter.
next_steps: Use a coding host with AUREN skill/MCP support, or attach bounded artifacts for discussion only.
Keep code changes, tests, approvals and merge authority inside AUREN.

xai_api.current_gap: No xAI API adapter, XAI_API_KEY allowlist, model catalog, response/tool-call normalizer, or live provider test exists.
next_steps: Add a dedicated xAI Responses adapter using https://api.x.ai/v1.
Implement remote MCP allowlists, approval handling, model capability declarations and cost/usage capture.
Test API-specific behavior; do not assume OpenAI feature parity or MCP approval parity.

mechanisms: xAI/Grok model APIs are separate from MCP client hosts
grok_build_cli.current_gap: No verified general-purpose Grok Build CLI client integration is established in this audit. xAI API model routing is also not wired in AUREN.
next_steps: Confirm the exact xAI/Grok product and supported MCP client protocol before adding an adapter.
Keep xAI inference-provider work separate from remote MCP client integration.

github_copilot.current_gap: VS Code remote MCP setup is documented. No live Copilot Agent-mode connection to the deployed AUREN service has been recorded.
next_steps: Register AUREN in .vscode/mcp.json.
Enable the server in Copilot Agent mode and verify OAuth/scoped tool discovery.
Run a disposable-repository task and verify AUREN remains the execution authority.

mechanisms: Remote MCP through other MCP-capable Visual Studio agent hosts
claude_visual_studio.current_gap: There is no verified first-party Claude Code extension for Microsoft Visual Studio. Claude Code CLI, VS Code extension and Claude Desktop remote connectors are separate supported paths. Visual Studio can still use AUREN through its GitHub Copilot MCP host, but that is not Claude Code.
next_steps: Use Claude Code CLI or VS Code extension for Anthropic coding-agent workflows.
Use Visual Studio Copilot Agent mode if Visual Studio is the required IDE.
Do not label Visual Studio Copilot MCP as Claude Code integration.

antigravity_cli.current_gap: Antigravity CLI remote MCP configuration is documented using serverUrl. AUREN is not yet connected to a live Antigravity CLI instance.
next_steps: Add serverUrl to ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json or workspace .agents/mcp_config.json.
Open /mcp and verify the remote server, OAuth and tool catalog.
Run a disposable workspace task and verify AUREN status/evidence/cancellation.

antigravity_ide.current_gap: Antigravity IDE supports custom remote MCP configuration. No AUREN installation or IDE live acceptance is recorded.
next_steps: Install the AUREN remote server through Antigravity MCP settings or custom mcp_config.json.
Complete OAuth and inspect the enabled tool list.
Run a guarded end-to-end task and verify AUREN remains the execution authority.

mechanisms: Custom MCP app if the desktop host exposes the same connector capability
chatgpt_desktop.current_gap: The current official custom MCP connection instructions are documented for ChatGPT web. Native ChatGPT desktop connector setup and OAuth linking have not been verified; use ChatGPT web for initial app registration and acceptance.
next_steps: Create and test the custom MCP app in ChatGPT web using the external OAuth provider.
Verify whether the installed ChatGPT desktop client exposes the same app/connector.
Do not claim desktop compatibility until a live desktop session passes tool discovery and authorization tests.

known_limits: MCP Tasks extension and server-sent event streaming are not implemented; long-running AUREN work uses explicit submit/status/evidence/cancel tools.
External OAuth provider must support the host-specific client registration and PKCE flow; no authorization server is bundled.

llm_provider_adapters.current_gap: The remote MCP service is model-host neutral: a supported MCP client can call AUREN regardless of which model generated the request. Direct inference routing is separate. ProviderFabric discovers the Claude, Codex, Gemini and Copilot CLIs; local fallback uses an Ollama-compatible loopback endpoint. Native direct HTTP adapters for Groq, xAI/Grok and other OpenAI-compatible APIs are not implemented.
next_steps: Keep MCP host compatibility separate from model-provider routing.
Add a governed OpenAI-compatible HTTP adapter with explicit HTTPS host allowlists, secret isolation, tool-call normalization, privacy routing and bounded budgets.
Add provider-specific conformance and live canary tests for Groq, xAI/Grok and any additional API provider before declaring support.
